references.text: The verse mentions the two goats as part of the sin offering for the people of Israel, which are the same goats presented in verse 7.
Describes what is to happen with the two goats after they are presented before the Lord's presence—one for the Lord and the other for Azazel.
Sacrificial animals were to be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting, before the Lord's presence, as described here.
The sin offering was to be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting, before the Lord's presence.
The priest was to present the one being cleansed before the Lord's presence at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Hebrews refers to the high priest who entered the Most Holy Place once a year with blood for his own sins and those of the people, which connects to the ritual of the Day of Atonement.
Christ entered the sanctuary with His own blood, fulfilling what the goat's blood on the Day of Atonement symbolized.
